scoreRule: 1 point per automatically scored item or sequence position, and 1 point per teacher-reviewed written response; unverified local proposal
description: Original shorter EN/B2 independent Listening assessment draft. Teacher review is required before any use.

variant.goal: Interpret an escalating attempt to control a tense celebration and the humour created by repeated interruptions.

gist.title: What conflict drives most of the scene?
options: The speaker must prevent trouble while the others keep interrupting him.
The speaker wants the guests to leave before the celebration.
The men are arranging a new business partnership.
A family is debating whether the ceremony should happen at all.
gist.why: The speaker's insistence on peace clashes with the interruptions and the threat of conflict.

gist.title: How does the scene use humour?
options: Everyone agrees with the rules but speaks very formally.
The conversation remains calm even when the orders become stricter.
Unexpected remarks interrupt an increasingly serious warning.
A storyteller retells a distant event with no effect on the group.
gist.why: Off-topic questions and protests break the speaker's attempt to maintain a stern warning.

detail.title: Why does the argument over clothing increase tension?
options: It reveals that the speaker has forgotten what event is taking place.
It shows that old divisions remain visible despite the celebration.
It proves that the guests have come to another ceremony.
It explains why one of the men needs a new uniform.
detail.why: The uniform-related complaint exposes hostility between groups attending the same event.

detail.title: What is the speaker trying to achieve by listing many prohibited actions?
options: He wants everyone to remember a previous agreement.
He is planning a series of games for the guests.
He is checking which activities the men enjoy.
He attempts to anticipate and control every possible source of trouble.
detail.why: The long prohibitions show that he expects disorder and wants to prevent it.

detail.title: What does the repeated final command communicate?
options: The speaker expects the men to obey despite their interruptions.
The speaker has decided his original instruction was unnecessary.
The group has already proved that there will be no trouble.
The speaker is inviting the men to argue about the rules.
detail.why: The repetition strengthens an order and makes his frustration apparent.

sequence: The speaker reminds the men of the importance of the occasion.
Interruptions force him to become more specific about forbidden behaviour.
He finishes with an emphatic warning intended to keep the peace.

facts.title: What type of event is the speaker trying to keep peaceful?
facts.criteria: Accept wedding or wedding celebration, not a generic party.

open.title: Explain why the speaker's aggressive manner is ironic given the aim of his instructions.
open.answer: He wants to prevent fighting, but he gives the order through threats, anger and repeated forceful commands.
open.criteria: Mention both the peaceful goal and at least one aggressive feature of his delivery.
